**Use the table for questions 1–2.** Language school, spring term.

| Course | Students | Fee per student (€) | Teacher cost (€) |
|---|---|---|---|
| English | 140 | 450 | 28,000 |
| German | 60 | 520 | 14,400 |
| French | 80 | 400 | 12,800 |
| Chinese | 30 | 600 | 9,000 |

questions.stem: Which course has the highest margin, measured as (fees − teacher cost) as a percentage of fees?
questions.explain: English 55.6%, German 53.8%, French 60.0%, Chinese 50.0%. English has the largest profit in euros, not the highest margin.

questions.stem: If the school raised the Chinese fee by 20% and, as a result, 5 fewer students enrolled, what would happen to Chinese fee revenue?
A translator charges €0.09 per word for the first 5,000 words of a job and €0.07 per word after that. Urgent jobs cost 25% more on the total. What is the price of an urgent 8,400-word job?
questions.explain: 450 + 3,400 × 0.07 (238) = 688 → × 1.25 = €860. €945 charges everything at 0.09; €800.50 applies the surcharge to the first band only.

questions.stem: What number comes next? 100, 95, 85, 70, 50, ?
By what percentage did Product P's sales increase from Q3 to Q4?
questions.explain: (39 − 27)/27 = 44.4%. 30.8% divides by Q4 (wrong base).

questions.stem: In which quarter was Product Q's share of the two products' combined sales highest?
questions.explain: Q1 42.9%, Q2 41.2%, Q3 55.0%, Q4 48.0%. Q4 has more units of Q, but not the highest share.

questions.stem: Product P sells for €45 and Product Q for €60. What was the combined revenue from both products in 2025?
questions.explain: P 120k × 45 = €5.40m; Q 108k × 60 = €6.48m; total €11.88m. 12.06 swaps the prices.

questions.stem: A restaurant bill is €184 before a 10% service charge. Four friends split the total so that three pay the same amount and the fourth pays that amount plus €20 for wine. How much does each of the three pay?
questions.explain: Total €202.40. 4x + 20 = 202.40 → x = €45.60. €41 forgets the service charge.

questions.stem: Each row follows the same rule. Row 1: 6, 3, 2. Row 2: 20, 4, 5. Row 3: 36, 9, ?
Which is the best estimate of 0.48 × 61,900 ÷ 2.95?
A train covers 210 km in 1 hour 45 minutes. What is its average speed?
40% of a company's staff work in Operations. 35% of all staff are women, and 30% of Operations staff are women. What percentage of the staff outside Operations are women?
questions.explain: Women in Operations = 0.4 × 0.3 = 12% of all staff. Outside: 35 − 12 = 23% of all staff, out of 60% → 38.3%. 23% forgets to change the denominator.

two.md: **Questions 13–14.** For each pair of statements, choose the option that best describes their relationship.

questions.stem:
No product in the clearance range can be returned. Some products bought online are in the clearance range.

**Conclusion:** Some products bought online cannot be returned.
questions.explain: The online products that are in the clearance range cannot be returned. It follows.

questions.stem:
All managers attended the leadership course. Some people who attended the leadership course were promoted.

**Conclusion:** Some managers were promoted.
questions.explain: Those promoted may be attendees who are not managers.

questions.stem:
Every analyst in the data team knows SQL. No one who knows SQL works in the reception team. Some members of the reception team work part-time.

Which statement must be true?
options: No analyst in the data team works in the reception team.
Everyone who knows SQL is an analyst in the data team.
Some analysts in the data team work part-time.
questions.explain: Analyst → SQL → not reception. B over-generalises: part-time staff outside reception may know SQL.

questions.stem:
Only invoices approved by a manager are paid within 30 days. Invoice 513 was not approved by a manager.

Which statement must be true?
options: Invoice 513 was not paid within 30 days.
Every approved invoice is paid within 30 days.
Invoice 513 will be approved next week.
questions.explain: "Only": being paid within 30 days requires approval. C reverses the rule.

questions.stem:
Six cars belonging to Gil, Hana, Iker, Jade, Kai and Luz are parked in spaces 1 to 6 in a row.
- Hana is in space 6.
- Jade is in the space immediately after Iker's.
- Iker is not in space 1.
- Gil is not next to Hana.
- Luz is in an even-numbered space.
- Kai is in a lower-numbered space than Gil.

Who is in space 3?
questions.explain: Gil can't be at 5 and needs Kai before him. Iker–Jade: 2–3, 3–4 or 4–5. Testing them, the only option is Kai 1, Luz 2, Gil 3, Iker 4, Jade 5, Hana 6.

questions.stem:
Five colleagues arrive at the office one after another.
- Nora arrives after Pia but before Omar.
- Quinn arrives last.
- Raul arrives immediately before Pia.

Who arrives second?
questions.explain: Raul, Pia, Nora, Omar, Quinn.

questions.stem:
Four teams (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta) finish a league in positions 1 to 4.
- Alpha finishes above Beta.
- Gamma finishes immediately below Delta.
- Beta does not finish last.
- Delta does not finish first.

Which team finishes third?
questions.explain: Delta–Gamma in 2–3 would leave Beta last. So Alpha 1, Beta 2, Delta 3, Gamma 4.

questions.stem:
"Our email campaign was opened by 40% of recipients, twice the industry average. The campaign was therefore a success."

Which assumption does the argument rely on?
options: The industry average is calculated correctly every year.
The next campaign will perform as well.
Recipients liked the design of the email.
The open rate is a good measure of a campaign's success.
The campaign was cheap to run.
questions.explain: The argument jumps from "many opened it" to "it was a success"; that only works if the open rate measures success.

questions.stem:
"Since the city lowered the speed limit to 30 km/h, road accidents have fallen by 25%. Lower speed limits reduce accidents."

Which statement, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Accidents are more common in winter.
Most drivers support the new limit.
Speed cameras were installed on two roads.
In the same period a new metro line opened and car traffic in the city fell by 30%.
questions.explain: Fewer cars alone could explain a 25% fall in accidents.

questions.stem:
A retailer claims that playing slower music in its stores increases sales.

Which statement, if true, most strengthens the claim?
options: Customers say they prefer slow music.
Sales rose after the change, during the Christmas season.
In a trial across 20 stores where the music tempo was switched at random from day to day, sales were 6% higher on slow-music days.
questions.explain: Random assignment by day isolates the effect of the music. B mixes the effect with Christmas.

questions.stem:
A box contains only red and blue pens. If you take out any 5 pens, you are certain to get at least 2 blue pens.

Which statement must be true?
options: There are at most 3 red pens.
There are more blue pens than red pens.
There are at least 5 blue pens.
There are at least 3 red pens.
questions.explain: With 4 red pens you could draw 4 red and 1 blue. B and D aren't certain (e.g. 3 red and 2 blue).

questions.stem:
At the conference, every speaker from Spain also chaired a panel. Nobody who chaired a panel attended the dinner. Elena attended the dinner.

Which statement must be true?
options: Elena was not a speaker from Spain.
Every panel chair was a speaker from Spain.
questions.explain: Dinner → didn't chair a panel → not a speaker from Spain. A and B claim more than can be deduced.

questions.stem:
(1) The company's website was down for eight hours.
(2) Online sales that day were the lowest of the year.
options: Statement 1 is the cause and statement 2 is its effect.
Statement 2 is the cause and statement 1 is its effect.
Both statements are effects of a common cause.
Both statements are effects of independent causes.
questions.explain: The website outage (1) causes the low sales (2).

questions.stem:
(1) Applications to nursing degrees rose by 30%.
(2) The previous year, the government announced higher salaries for nurses.
options: Statement 1 is the cause and statement 2 is its effect.
Statement 2 is the cause and statement 1 is its effect.
Both statements are effects of a common cause.
Both statements are effects of independent causes.
questions.explain: The announced pay rise (2) increases applications (1).

questions.stem:
Home-working allowance: employees receive €40 a month if they work from home on at least 8 days that month, or €60 instead if they work from home on more than 15 days. Part-time employees receive half of these amounts.

A part-time employee worked from home on 16 days in March. How much does she receive?
questions.explain: 16 > 15 → €60, half for part-time = €30.

questions.stem:
Event tickets: €200 if booked before 1 March, €260 otherwise. Members get 15% off. Groups of 5 or more get 20% off each ticket. The member and group discounts cannot be combined.

A member books on 10 March for herself and 4 colleagues. What is the lowest price she can pay for her own ticket?
questions.explain: Standard price (after 1 March). Best non-combinable discount: 20% group → €208. €176.80 combines both; €160 uses the early-bird price.

questions.stem: Which statements can be concluded from the chart? **Select all that apply.**
options: North was above 90% in every month.
The gap between the two warehouses was largest in January.
North delivered more orders on time than South.
questions.explain: A ✔. B ✗ flat in April and down in June. C ✔ 93 > 91. D ✔ 5 points (Feb 4, Jun 3). E ✗ no volumes given.

questions.stem:
Employee engagement survey:

| Department | Respondents | Engaged |
|---|---|---|
| Sales | 80 | 60% |
| Tech | 120 | 75% |
| Admin | 50 | 40% |

Which statements can be concluded from the data? **Select all that apply.**
options: Tech has the largest number of engaged respondents.
Overall engagement across all respondents is 58.3%.
Overall engagement across all respondents is 63.2%.
questions.explain: Engaged: 48, 90, 20 → 158/250 = 63.2%. A ✔. B ✗ that is the simple average. C ✔. D ✗ no time series. E ✔.

questions.stem: What percentage of total sales came from the East region?

Website conversion funnel, one month:

| Step | Users |
|---|---|
| Visited the site | 20,000 |
| Viewed a product | 8,000 |
| Added to cart | 2,000 |
| Purchased | 600 |

What percentage of users who added something to their cart went on to purchase?
questions.explain: 600/2,000 = 30%. 3% divides by all visits; 7.5% by those who viewed a product.

questions.stem: Every employee in a team of 10 receives a €2,000 pay rise. What happens to the mean and the standard deviation of the team's salaries?
options: The mean increases by €2,000 and the standard deviation is unchanged.
The mean is unchanged and the standard deviation increases.
questions.explain: Adding a constant shifts the mean and leaves the spread unchanged.

questions.stem: In a town, mean household income is €52k and median household income is €38k. What does this suggest about the distribution of income?
options: It is skewed to the right, with a small number of very high incomes.
Half of households earn more than €52k.
It is skewed to the left, with many very low incomes.
questions.explain: Mean well above the median → a long tail to the right.

questions.stem: The unemployment rate rose from 8% to 10%. Which statement is correct?
options: It rose by 2 percentage points, an increase of 25%.
questions.explain: 10 − 8 = 2 percentage points; 2/8 = 25%.

questions.stem: In a sales file, 5% of rows have no value in the Region field. A regional sales chart drops these rows, so its total is lower than the company's total sales. What is the best approach?
options: Leave the chart as it is.
Show the missing rows as an "Unassigned" category and investigate why the region is missing.
Spread the missing sales equally across regions without saying so.
Delete the rows from the company total too.
Assign them all to the largest region.
questions.explain: Make the gap visible and find the cause. C and E invent data.

questions.stem: A form asks for "Number of employees" as free text. Answers include "50-100", "75" and "about 60". What is the best way to improve the data?
options: Replace all answers with the median.
Use predefined ranges or a validated numeric field in the form, and map the existing answers to ranges.
questions.explain: Prevent at the source (validation) and standardise what has already been collected.

questions.stem: A table of percentages that should describe a whole adds up to 101%. What is the most likely reason?
options: A data entry error in one row.
questions.explain: Rounding each percentage can make the total 99% or 101%.

questions.stem: You want to compare sales of 12 product categories in a single year. Which chart is most appropriate?
questions.explain: Comparing categories → sorted bars. A pie with 12 slices is hard to read.

questions.stem: Two charts are placed side by side to compare monthly sales in two regions. One chart's vertical axis runs from 0 to 100 and the other's from 0 to 1,000, but the bars look similar in height. What is the problem?
options: The months are in the wrong order.
The different scales make the two regions look similar when their sales are very different.
questions.explain: Charts being compared need the same scale.
